title: Brass bands in the 1920s: Eureka and Pacific
summary: Howard played in the Eureka and Pacific brass bands, took over leading Eureka when Wilson fell ill.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: So this is real, too. Get out. What about in the 20s? Did you work with any brass bands

back then? Yeah, well I worked with practically all the brass bands in the 20s. Before depression? Yeah. Before 1929? I worked then, and during the depression I made practically all my living off of funerals. Who did you work with? What were the names of some of the brass bands in the 20s? Well, the original Eureka brass band. I started playing in the band with Wilson, Lita, Schatz was the second man, but after I got into the band, and Wilson taking sick, well I started leading the band. Wilson and Johnny, his brother,
it was their band. What's Wilson's first name? I didn't

get it. Oh, I know his brother was named Johnny Wilson. I just remember what his name was. His brother was Johnny Wilson, and old man Bob was playing in that band at that time. Ray, the bass player, he was playing trombone at that time. Big Connie, they were playing. I played that band, and I played with the Pacific band with Rene, with Rene was the lead, and I don't know, he quit or something. I led that band with Talbot. He was playing trumpet. And Edgar Mosley, he was playing the bass drum. I can't recall exactly all the fellas in that band. Pacific brass band. Brass band, yeah,
a brass band at that time. Did they have a clarinet player?
Yeah, they had a clarinet player. George used to play a lot of times with us in that band,
and he was playing the bass band. Let's see, alto player? Let's see, I'm trying to think of who the alto players were in that band.
In the brass band? In the Pacific. In the Pacific.
Alto horn. Manny Gabriel. Yeah. An alto saxophone? Alto saxophone. I thought maybe they had an alto horn there.
Oh. Old Man Bob used to mostly play with all the bands that Old Man Bob ran. He played alto horn. Then they had a fellow called Flowers, he used to play at the alto horn, the peck horn,

in that band too. Where was he from, Flowers? The West Indian. That you make our song. That's right. Let's see. Got to check all this. Uh. When the secretary comes, we got your name and an index here. We want to check that over. Let me see. So you played with the Pacific, Eureka?

That's right, Tuxedo, when Eddie Jackson takes over. Yeah. I played with Eureka. Who was this guy, Gassoon? Gassoon was a banjo man. I met him on my way coming up, but he had to go to the clinic. Other than that I'd have brought him over. Well who was? I mean Gassoon, his name is Joe Phillip. But did he play in the brass band? No, no, he played in the band. He played with Chris and with me, most of the time with Rene and different fellas.
Let me find something from the interview that Bill did with you. Hold on a second. When you came into the Eureka, what part did they give you?
Uh, the second part. That's the first in the brass band. I was in the middle.
I see. Well who decided about what part you should take?

Well, about the part I should have taken, it was undecided. They didn't know I could read. And Ernest Rogers played the drum. He the one that brought me in. They needed a man to play, so he recommended me, which he used to play in the brass band, in the Pacific band. And he recommended me to Wilson, so we got there, I could hear him talk, and they didn't know. This is one of them kids that's like, a kid playing, a kid somebody, or something like a kid. And so after they gave me the part and I played all right, well they take me in the band. Then they put Shot Spike on the second, put me with Wilson, and after Wilson taken sick, and I led the band for a long time. The man, he played a lot of times, solos with different fellas, Huntley Gordet. What's his name? Huntley Gordet. Huntley Gordet.
Yeah. You know what I heard of him? Somewhere. Who else did he play with?
Well, Luis the man taught him. He had his own band. He died in California somewhere.

Is that the guy that played with Jack Carey? Yeah, he played with a lot of those things. He did. He would play with the writing bands, going there? Yeah. Yeah. What about your father? Did he play music? No, nobody in the family played music at that time. Did they sing? Well yeah, but there's church members,
